findings.body: Teardown deletes `alias` rather than the provider created in that iteration, leaving the generated IDPs in the shared test realm and allowing them to pollute later tests or make cleanup fail against an unrelated fixture.
findings.failure_mode: Test teardown does not remove the fixtures created by the loop.
findings.impact: Teardown deletes `alias` rather than the provider created in that iteration, leaving the generated IDPs in the shared test realm and allowing them to pollute later tests or make cleanup fail against an unrelated fixture.
findings.root_cause: The cleanup resource is looked up with the literal string `"alias"` instead of the generated alias.
findings.suggested_fix: Register cleanup for the alias created in the current iteration, for example `get("idp-alias-" + i)::remove`.
findings.title: Cleanup for generated login IDPs targets a nonexistent literal alias
findings.trigger: After any iteration that creates `idp-alias-0` through `idp-alias-19`, the test teardown executes its registered cleanup actions.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 381 verbatim shows `get("alias")::remove` inside a loop that creates IDPs with aliases `idp-alias-0` through `idp-alias-19`. The literal string `"alias"` does not match any created alias, so cleanup will fail to remove the actual IDPs, leaving test fixtures behind. This is a real bug introduced by the patch.
